messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: problem with tar
parts:
Hi, 
I am seeing this error bootstrapping

> bootstrap(sourcePackagePaths=c("../rmr2/pkg/", "pkg/")) 
Already up to date
Installing rmr2 (3.0.0) ... sh: /usr/bin/gnutar: No such file or directory
sh: /usr/bin/gnutar: No such file or directory
Error in system(cmd, intern = TRUE) : error in running command
In addition: Warning message:
In untar(src, exdir = target, compressed = "gzip") :
  ‘/usr/bin/gnutar -xf '/Users/antonio/Projects/Revolution/plyrmr/packrat.sources/rmr2/rmr2_3.0.0.tar.gz' -C '/var/folders/_p/1gx4vy311_x4syn2xq6f2xtc0000gr/T//RtmpsTtJ3H'’ returned error code 127


It is true that I don't have gnutar. I installed XCode cmd line tools. Googling around I see problems with gnutar in mavericks. Proposed solution is to run xcode-select --install, which fails too. Any ideas? Thanks


Antonio

messages.author: 5893d17d64b5b0c2
messages.subject: Re: problem with tar
parts:
Hi Antonio, 

Yes, this is generally a problem with R and Mavericks. By default R uses /usr/bin/gnutar on OS X, but gnutar was removed in Mavericks.

The safest workaround for now is to add the following to your .Renviron file: 

TAR=/usr/bin/tar 

We're considering an automatic workaround here (especially if R core doesn't fix this); this issue in Github has more information:

https://github.com/rstudio/packrat/issues/37

Jonathan.
